$comment: Analyzer rules for the ScubaGear Config Analyzer (Start-SCuBAConfigAnalyzer). This is the single home for everything the analyzer needs that is NOT already in another schema: friendly requirement-path names, the product-key casing map, the named Graph operations it performs (resolved to real URLs via ScubaGearApiCatalog.json), and the rules for how to interpret conditionalAccessPolicy requirements in ScubaGearResultsBaselineSchema.json. The engine (ScubaConfigAnalyzerEngine.psm1) is a generic interpreter of this file - to add products, API calls, exclusion types or CA conditions, edit THIS file + the baseline schema, not the .psm1. The canonical config-file structure/regex is defined once in ../../ScubaConfig/ScubaConfigSchema.json and is not duplicated here.
title: ScubaGear Config Analyzer
description: Scan your M365 tenant and see exactly what to change to pass ScubaGear

productMap._comment: Maps the analyzer product key (lowercase; matches ScubaGear ProductNames and baselineValidations keys) to how the product appears in a ScubaResults JSON (resultsKey, under .Results/.Summary), in a ScubaGear config YAML (configKey), and a friendly displayName for the UI. Replaces the hardcoded product hashtable that used to live in the engine.

apiOperations._comment: Named Graph operations the analyzer performs. 'cmdlet' is looked up in ScubaGearApiCatalog.json (the single source of truth for API paths + least permissions) to build the real URL - nothing here hardcodes a URL. resultKind: collection (list, paged) | byId (single item, {id} substituted) | byAppId (single service principal by appId). 'select' -> $select query; 'nameProperties' -> ordered display-name fallbacks for lookups.

conditionalAccessAnalysis._comment: Rules the engine uses to interpret a conditionalAccessPolicy control's validationLogic.requirements (from ScubaGearResultsBaselineSchema.json) against tenant CA policies. All paths are camelCase, relative to a CA policy object; the engine navigates them case-insensitively so both ScubaResults (PascalCase) and raw Graph (camelCase) policies work.

scopeGates._comment: A policy is only a candidate to make a control pass if it targets the scope the requirement demands. A gate applies ONLY when the requirement asks for requiredValue at conditionPath; then the policy must also have requiredValue at policyPath or it is out of scope (persona/admin-scoped policies are dropped). Exclusions do not affect scope.

relevanceSignals._comment: A policy is only analyzed for a control if it is RELEVANT (about that control). arrayMatch: requirement + policy arrays overlap - match=all means the policy must contain every required value, match=any means at least one. grantControls: relevant when the requirement's grant controls match the policy's, but only via the enabled sub-signals (anyOf alternatives / an authentication-strength id) - builtInControls-only is off by default so broad 'block' policies do not over-match.

exclusionDetectors._comment: Config-waivable exclusions ScubaGear supports via CapExclusions. Each detector reads policyPath off the policy; when present it is reported as a waivable WARNING (add to config to pass) and collected under the config field. requiresExclusionType gates the detector to controls whose exclusionField matches (so guest/app waivers only apply where CapExclusions is supported). scopeRequirement limits a detector to controls that demand a scope (apps only when the requirement targets All cloud apps; guests only when it targets All users). valueKind idList = array of ids; csvOrArray = comma-string or array. unsupportedIsError: when the control does NOT support this exclusion type but the policy still has the exclusion, emit a setting ERROR instead.

rules.suggestion: If justified (break-glass accounts): Add to CapExclusions Users in ScubaConfig
If justified: Add to CapExclusions Groups in ScubaConfig
If justified: Add to CapExclusions Applications in ScubaConfig
If justified: Add to CapExclusions GuestUserTypes in ScubaConfig
rules.unsupportedMessage: Policy excludes guest/external user types ({values}); this control does not support guest exclusions - remove them from the policy.

displayNameLookup._comment: After a live scan, resolve friendly display names for the excluded principals/apps at these policy paths, via the named apiOperation, to annotate the generated YAML. GUIDs only; failures per id are ignored.
